blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Uniform frame sampling can miss brief evidence in sparse-event videos when the VLM sees only K frames. We propose EARS (Evidence-Aware Retrieval via Sound and motion), a training-free, query-free front-end that ranks frames using optical-flow motion and audio energy, then applies temporal non-maximum suppression for diversity. The evidence score alone has frame-level AP 0.39; used only to select frames for the VLM, EARS with temporal diversity reaches localization AP 0.94, compared with 0.88 under Uniform sampling. In the updated matched study, at K = 1 EARS reaches XD-subset F1 0.660 versus 0.614 for centered Uniform (the paired interval includes zero); earlier backbone studies use separate protocols. On mostly-silent UCF-Crime, however, EARS slightly trails Uniform. A single configuration is used across both benchmarks; the new controls do not repeat the original held-out search. EARS therefore targets low-budget videos whose salient evidence aligns with motion or audio; on dense narratives or stealthy events, uniform or semantic selection remains preferable, and cheap modality statistics cannot reliably route between them. Code: https://github.com/mikeslin-ir/EARS

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Video understanding requires reasoning over long temporal sequences, where informative content is often sparse and unevenly distributed. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) [ 14 , 35 , 16 , 25 ] have achieved strong performance on multimodal reasoning tasks, but their application to long videos remains computationally expensive, since VLM context capacity grows much slower than video length [ 36 , 11 ] .
blocks.zh: 视频理解需要对较长的时间序列进行推理,因为信息内容往往稀少,分布不均。 近期的视觉语言模型(VLMs)[14,35,16,25]在多式联运推理任务上取得了很强的性能,但由于VLM上下文容量的增长比视频长度慢得多[36,11],因此其对长视频的应用仍然在计算上昂贵.

blocks.en:
A common approach is to sample a fixed number of frames uniformly across time. This strategy implicitly assumes that useful information is evenly distributed. However, real-world videos violate this assumption. In many scenarios, such as surveillance and safety monitoring [ 22 , 28 ] , important events occur only briefly, while the majority of frames contain little relevant information.
This mismatch leads to a fundamental inefficiency: processing more frames does not necessarily improve reasoning if those frames lack meaningful evidence. Under limited frame budgets, uniform sampling may miss critical evidence entirely [ 31 , 23 ] .
blocks.zh:
一种常见的做法是在一段时间内对固定数量的框架进行统一抽样。 该战略隐含地假定有用的信息得到平均分发。 然而,真实世界的视频违反了这一假设. 在许多情景中,如监视和安全监测[22,28],重要事件仅短暂发生,而大多数帧包含的相关信息很少.
这种不匹配导致根本效率低下:如果这些框架缺乏有意义的证据,处理更多框架不一定能改善推理。 根据有限的框架预算,统一的抽样可能完全错过关键证据[31,23]。

blocks.en:
In this work, we focus on sparse-event video reasoning under tight frame budgets , and argue that in this regime video reasoning should operate on evidence rather than frames . Instead of treating all frames equally, models should identify and prioritize temporally localized, information-rich regions.
To this end, we propose a training-free multimodal evidence selection front-end that leverages cheap, modality-intrinsic motion and audio signals to estimate a per-frame evidence score. These complementary modalities capture visual dynamics and acoustic activity, enabling detection of salient evidence without any learning or task-specific supervision (Sec. 3 ). In contrast to query-aware localizers [ 31 , 26 ] or learned keyframe samplers [ 23 ] , our method requires no additional VLM forward passes and no training, and is complementary to such methods: it can be combined with semantic/query-aware signals or used as a cheap fallback when those signals are unavailable.
blocks.zh:
也认为影片应该用证据而非框架。 模型不应平等地对待所有框架,而应确定时间上本地化、信息丰富的区域并确定优先次序。
为此,我们建议采用无培训的多式联运证据选择前端,利用廉价、模式内在的运动和音频信号,估计每个框架的证据得分。 这些互补模式能够捕捉视觉动态和声学活动,从而能够在没有任何学习或特定任务监督的情况下探测显著证据(第3节)。 与了解查询的本地化器[31,26]或学到的键框采样器[23]不同,我们的方法不需要额外的VLM前传通行证,也不需要训练,并且是对这种方法的补充:它可以与语义/query-aware信号结合使用,或者在没有这些信号时用作廉价的回落.

blocks.en:
We instantiate this idea as EARS (Evidence-Aware Retrieval via Sound and motion), a lightweight, training-free front-end that selects frames from high-evidence regions and feeds them to a downstream VLM (Fig. 2 ). Unlike query-aware or learned selectors [ 31 , 23 , 26 ] , EARS runs zero-shot per video : no query, no auxiliary VLM passes, no learned scorer.
Experiments on XD-Violence [ 28 ] and UCF-Crime [ 22 ] (Sec. 4 ) show that EARS’s gain is sharply conditional on the regime: it strongly improves XD-Violence when audio-visual evidence aligns with the anomaly, but slightly trails Uniform on mostly-silent, visually subtle UCF-Crime . On the dense-narrative EgoSchema benchmark uniform sampling is also stronger, confirming that EARS is most appropriate when evidence is sparse, temporally localized, and correlated with motion or audio — not a universal frame selector.
blocks.zh:
我们即刻将这个想法作为EARS(通过声音和运动获取证据-软件),这是一个轻量级,无训练的前端,它从高证据区域中选择帧,并提供给下游的VLM(图2). 与了解查询或学习选手[31,23,26]不同的是,EARS每部视频运行零镜头:没有查询,没有辅助VLM通过,没有学习计分器.
有关XD-暴力的实验[28]和UCF-Crime[22](第4节)显示,EARS的得益完全取决于该政权:当视听证据与异常现象一致时,它大大改进了XD-暴力,但略微跟踪了大多是低沉的、视觉微妙的UCF-Crime。 在密集的叙述式EgoSchema基准统一取样上,也更加有力,证实当证据稀少、时间定位和与运动或音频相关——而不是通用框架选择器——时,EARS最合适。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Video-Language Models
blocks.zh: 2.1 视频语言模型

blocks.en:
Recent video-language models (VLMs) extend image-language pretraining to the
temporal domain by sampling a fixed number of frames from an input video and
feeding their visual tokens to a large language model (LLM).
Representative systems include VideoChat [ 14 ] , Video-LLaMA [ 35 ] , Video-LLaVA [ 16 ] and Qwen2-VL [ 25 ] , which now achieve strong performance on
short-form video QA and captioning.
For long-form videos, recent work either extrapolates the LLM context
length [ 36 ] or designs memory mechanisms to summarize the full
sequence [ 11 ] , both of which still rely on uniformly sampled
frames as the underlying visual stream.
Standardized evaluations such as MVBench [ 15 ] report that
performance degrades sharply when the frame budget is small, indicating that which frames are shown matters as much as how many.
We share this motivation but, in contrast to methods that scale up the
context window, focus on selecting a small, information-dense subset of
frames before any VLM computation is performed.

blocks.en: 2.2 Frame Sampling and Keyframe Selection
blocks.zh: 2.2 框架取样和关键框架选择

blocks.en:
Uniform sampling is the de-facto default in VLM pipelines because of its
simplicity, but it implicitly assumes information is evenly distributed in
time.
Earlier work on adaptive video recognition such as
ClipBERT [ 13 ] and AdaFrame [ 29 ] already showed that
sparse, content-aware sampling can match or beat dense sampling under tight
budgets.
For modern multimodal LLMs, SeViLA [ 31 ] chains a BLIP-2-based localizer and an answerer to find query-relevant
keyframes; AKS [ 23 ] formulates keyframe selection as an
optimization that jointly maximizes prompt relevance and temporal
coverage; M-LLM-FS [ 12 ] scores frames with a multimodal
LLM; and VideoTree [ 27 ] builds a hierarchical CLIP-based
frontier over the video.
Agent-style approaches such as VideoAgent [ 26 ] iteratively
query a vision tool to gather evidence.
Recent training-free selectors reduce this overhead while retaining
semantic guidance. WFS-SB [ 7 ] detects wavelet-smoothed
semantic boundaries before relevance-aware allocation;
EFS [ 6 ] partitions videos with DINO features and selects a
query-relevant anchor per event; and MEC [ 5 ] constructs one
query-conditioned evidence-to-context ranking reusable across budgets.
KeyScore [ 17 ] combines caption similarity, temporal
representativeness, and contextual drop impact to score frames, together
with spatio-temporal adaptive clustering for compact, diverse proposals.
Complementing selection methods, STEC [ 18 ] is a
reference-free diagnostic metric that evaluates a sampled frame set through
spatial entropy, temporal coverage, and non-redundancy without claiming to
predict downstream task accuracy.
These methods deliver clear gains, but all semantic selectors above
consume a task query and a learned image/video representation; several
also call an LLM/VLM during selection.
Our work is complementary rather than competing: we use cheap,
modality-intrinsic signals (motion and audio energy) that require no
learning and no extra VLM forward passes, providing a training-free
front-end for the sparse-event, low-budget regime. The same selected
frames can be fed to any off-the-shelf VLM, and the evidence score is
additive with semantic/query-aware signals (e.g. CLIP/SigLIP
similarity) when those are available — see Sec. 4.4 .

blocks.en: 2.3 Efficient Video Understanding
blocks.zh: 2.3 有效的视频理解

blocks.en:
A parallel line of work reduces computation inside the model rather
than at the input.
Token-level methods such as TokenLearner [ 21 ] and Token
Merging [ 3 ] dynamically prune or merge spatio-temporal tokens
during the forward pass.
These techniques are largely orthogonal to frame selection and can be
combined with our method: we reduce the number of frames before tokenization, while token pruning further compresses the remaining
representation.
We view our IC mechanism (Sec. 3 ) as an explicit, temporal
counterpart of token merging operating on the evidence axis.

blocks.en:
A recent wave of audio-visual token-compression methods—OmniZip [ 24 ] , EchoingPixels [ 10 ] , and
OmniSIFT [ 8 ] —prunes or merges multimodal tokens after the encoder to fit long videos into a fixed context.
These are post-encoder operations and are orthogonal to, and
combinable with, EARS, which acts pre-encoder : it decides which
frames enter the VLM at all, so no encoder pass is spent on frames that
are later discarded. On the selection side, BOLT [ 19 ] similarly finds uniform sampling suboptimal for long video, but scores
frames by query–frame similarity, whereas our signal is query-free and
modality-intrinsic. Finally, our “evidence” framing connects to
temporally-grounded VLMs [ 33 ] and grounded multi-hop
VideoQA [ 4 ] , which localize supporting moments for a
question; EARS instead surfaces salient moments without a
question, as a cheap default when no query is available.

blocks.en:
Audio and visual streams have long been recognized as complementary for
event and anomaly detection.
On the surveillance side, UCF-Crime [ 22 ] and
XD-Violence [ 28 ] are standard weakly-supervised benchmarks,
with the latter providing aligned audio for every clip.
Recent methods such as MACIL-SD [ 30 ] and UR-DMU [ 38 ] exploit audio-visual cues with multiple-instance learning and dual memory
banks to localize abnormal snippets.
These works treat audio-visual fusion as the end task : produce a
binary anomaly score per snippet.
We reuse the same intuition—that motion and audio energy spike around
salient events—but use these signals as a front-end for evidence
selection that is decoupled from any particular downstream task and from
the anomaly label space.

blocks.en: 2.5 Summary
blocks.zh: 2.5 总结

blocks.en:
Prior work either (i) consumes uniformly sampled frames with
ever-larger VLMs, (ii) trains query-aware or agent-based localizers,
or (iii) fuses audio and vision to directly produce anomaly labels.
Recent selectors increasingly avoid training and repeated VLM calls,
but remain query-conditioned and vision-centric. EARS instead combines training-free , single-pass , query-free , and audio-visual selection. The evidence score is additive with
semantic/query-aware signals (CLIP/SigLIP, learned rankers) and
serves as a cheap default when those signals are unavailable.

blocks.en: 4.7 Discussion

blocks.en:
EARS targets tight budgets where sparse events align with motion or
audio; Uniform catches up as K K grows and wins on dense-narrative,
audio-silent EgoSchema. A hybrid can anneal toward Uniform at larger
budgets, while stealthy events require a semantic third channel.
Complete ablations, failures, efficiency, and routing analyses appear in
the supplementary.
Together, the stress tests distinguish robustness from universality.
Flow replacement and backbone transfer preserve the tight-budget XD
effect, while the held-out grid removes test-set configuration choice.
Conversely, EgoSchema and the failed per-video router show that cheap
signals cannot decide when semantic evidence is required. Query-aware
selectors should therefore be preferred when a task query is available;
EARS occupies the complementary setting where no query or selector
encoder is available and the frame budget is the binding constraint.

EARS is grounded in the assumption that salient events are temporally
sparse and visually or acoustically distinguishable. On dense-narrative
